newsitem.title: USA: Most natgas futures end up on short covering.
newsitem.headline: Most natgas futures end up on short covering.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures mostly ended higher Thursday in an active session, with front months driven by technical buying and short covering on reports of strong gains in the cash, sources said.

October, which expires Tuesday, rallied 9.5 cents to close at $2.063 per million British thermal units. November settled 5.3 cents higher at $2.257. Other deferreds ended mixed, with 1998s losing ground.
"It looked like another day of short squeeze, but it may have run its course. The market is overbought and we could see lower numbers soon," said one East Coast trader.
Traders said technical buying kicked in when October broke psychological resistance at $2 early in the session.
While some doubted the rally would carry much further with more mild weather ahead to temper demand, others said attractive cash-to-futures spreads should keep storage injections high.
Chartists pegged next October resistance in the $2.15-20 area, with support still at the $1.88-1.885 gap.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices jumped five to 10 cents Thursday to the mid-to-high $1.80s, with swing gas at Henry Hub talked near the mid-$1.90s. Midcon pipes firmed about five cents to the mid-$1.70s. New York city gate gas was five to 10 cents higher in the $2.10-2.15 area.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip jumped 5.2 cents to $2.154. NYMEX said 60,282 Henry Hub contracts traded, up sharply from Wednesday's revised tally of 28,506.
NYMEX October Permian natgas closed nine cents higher at $1.74, while deferreds were untraded. NYMEX said 15 Permian contracts traded versus 29 on Wednesday.
NYMEX October Permian natgas expires Thursday, Sept 26.
On the KCBT, October finished four cents higher at $1.81, while deferreds ended up by one to 3.5 cents. The East/West spread widened by 5.5 cents to 25.3 cents (NYMEX premium).
KCBT October natgas expires Wednesday, Sept 25.
